rationale: All three review lenses ran; acceptance lens confirms every EPMCDME-13675 AC (AC1-AC6) is satisfied. No blocking (critical/major) findings surfaced by triage. Six deferred non-blocking concerns are recorded as follow-ups: (1) add a defensive watchdog on the drain loop; (2) reject empty <bash-input></bash-input> to avoid a bare '!' entry; (3) extend the <bash-stdout>/<bash-stderr> filter to array content shapes; (4) consider whether <bash-input> under a tool_result parent should be excluded from isSyntheticUserPrompt; (5) tighten the T3 test guard from `< 10` to `messages.length`; (6) audit the partial-write behavior of the drain loop (pre-existing single-write also has this weakness). Four other blind-lens concerns were dismissed as cosmetic (duplicate T1 name, silent filter matches existing precedent, monotonicity check is complemented by fixture assertion, fixture visibility is a diff-window artifact) or pre-existing (hardcoded assistant UUID). Two of the three lenses ran fully clean on the diff's substance; the blind lens surfaced defensive concerns none of which fail the acceptance criteria or introduce a regression.

business_review.item: AC1: !bash commands recorded in local session log
business_review.notes: extractCommand unwraps <bash-input> to !<cmd>; drain loop persists User entry per bash turn

business_review.item: AC2: Multiple bash commands captured in correct order
business_review.notes: T3 asserts ['!ls -al','!pwd','!whoami'] in that order; integration test asserts 4 records with monotonic history_index

business_review.item: AC3: Following code prompt does not lose bash entries
business_review.notes: Drain loop writes all pending turns per invocation; T3 asserts both bash turns and the follow-up question+answer land in history

business_review.item: AC4: Log distinguishes user prompts, bash commands, assistant responses
business_review.notes: Bash User entries carry `!` prefix; regular prompts are plain text; Assistant role for responses

business_review.item: AC5: Claude Code execution behavior unchanged
business_review.notes: Only logging path changed (processor + tests); no changes to session adapter, hooks, sub-agent parsing, metrics, or downstream sync

business_review.item: AC6: Regression testing covers !ls -al, !ls -al trailing-space, mixed session
business_review.notes: Six new unit tests (T1 single + T1 trailing-space + T2 stdout + T2 stderr + T4 triple + T3 mixed) plus updated integration test

standards_review.notes: Commit subject `fix(agents): log !bash commands ... (EPMCDME-13675)` follows Conventional Commits; type=fix, scope=agents (allowed), ticket suffix
New imports use .js extensions; explicit return types on new API surface; `any` uses are confined to existing test-fixture patterns
No secrets or credentials touched; new logger.info line surfaces only turn count, not message content
New unit tests reuse the existing user()/assistant()/ts() factories and (proc as any).transformMessages() private-access pattern established in the file
